bib.title: Camels in a Changing Climate: Enhancing LM Adaptation with TÜLU 2

question: How much do better base models, a new instruction mix, DPO, and QLoRA improve open LLaMA-2 instruction-tuned models over TÜLU 1?
contributions: TÜLU-V2-mix, an improved collection of high-quality instruction datasets
TÜLU 2, LLAMA-2 models finetuned on the V2 mixture
TÜLU 2+DPO, trained with DPO, including the largest DPO-trained model to date (70B)
CODE TÜLU 2, CODE LLAMA models finetuned on the V2 mix

method.summary: LLaMA-2 (7B/13B/70B) and Code Llama (7B/13B/34B) are fully finetuned on a 326,154-sample V2 mix, then DPO-trained on binarized UltraFeedback with Zephyr-Beta hyperparameters. QLoRA is compared with full finetuning. Evaluation uses an 8-task suite plus MT-Bench with GPT-4-0613 as judge.
method.task: instruction tuning and preference optimisation (DPO) of LLMs

datasets.name: TÜLU-V2-mix
datasets.source: FLAN 50,000; CoT 50,000; Open Assistant 1 7,708; ShareGPT 114,046; GPT4-Alpaca 20,000; Code-Alpaca 20,022; LIMA 1,030; WizardLM Evol-Instruct V2 30,000; Open-Orca 30,000; Science literature 7,544; Hardcoded 140
datasets.preprocessing: filtered samples referencing other LLM systems (GPT-4, Open Assistant, Claude); Dolly removed; FLAN downsampled; max length 8,192 tokens (20 samples truncated vs 63,900 at 2,048); mean length 1097 tokens

datasets.name: UltraFeedback (filtered, binarized, as Zephyr-Beta)
datasets.preprocessing: filtered and binarized; contains TruthfulQA prompts so TruthfulQA is omitted for DPO models

datasets.name: MMLU, GSM8k, BBH, TydiQA GoldP, Codex-Eval (HumanEval 164 problems), ToxiGen, TruthfulQA (818 q), AlpacaEval (805 prompts), MT-Bench (80 questions with followups)

training.objective: SFT (2 epochs); DPO on UltraFeedback; QLoRA SFT variant
training.hardware: 256-chip TPU v3 pod (512-chip for 70B DPO); QLoRA on internal A100 80GB cluster
training.compute: 70B DPO: 512-core TPUv3, three epochs in approximately 7 days

other.qlora_layers: all attention and feedforward linear layers

inference.decoding: Codex-Eval sampled; ToxiGen and TruthfulQA greedy; AlpacaEval up to 8192 tokens, no stop sequences
inference.prompting: MMLU 0-shot; GSM8k 8-shot CoT; BBH 3-shot CoT; TydiQA 1-shot GoldP; TruthfulQA 6 in-context examples

metrics.name: AlpacaEval win rate
metrics.definition: % of generations GPT-4 (alpaca_eval_gpt4 annotator, GPT-4-0613) prefers over Davinci-003

metrics.name: MT-Bench
metrics.definition: single-answer grading by GPT-4-0613 over 160 responses

metrics.name: Average
metrics.definition: naive average over tasks; ToxiGen as 100-x

metrics.name: ToxiGen
metrics.definition: % generations a roberta-large classifier deems toxic

eval.protocol: single runs reported, no seeds or significance tests stated; GPT-4 judge

evidence.quote: was trained on a 512-core TPUv3, completing three epochs in approximately 7 days

results.claim: DPO raises AlpacaEval win rate at 70B
results.setup: LLaMA-2 70B, V2 SFT then DPO on UltraFeedback

results.claim: DPO gains on AlpacaEval at all sizes (+11.2 at 7B, +10.6 at 13B, +8.5 at 70B)

results.setup: 70B TÜLU 2+DPO vs TÜLU 2; 7B unchanged (6.30 to 6.27), 13B 6.70 to 7.00

results.claim: DPO with Zephyr-Beta hyperparameters is stable at 70B; largest publicly released DPO model
results.quote: DPO training is stable at large scales.

results.claim: DPO sharply cuts multilingual TydiQA at 70B (-17.8) and 13B (-13.5)
DPO increases output verbosity (AlpacaEval avg output length 1011 to 1414 at 70B)
results.table: Table 4, row 70B TÜLU 2+DPO, column Avg. Output Length

results.claim: DPO leaves most capability metrics roughly unchanged
results.quote: This suggests that DPO training does not significantly change model capabilities.
results.note: 70B average drops 73.8 to 72.1 mostly from TydiQA

results.claim: V2 mix beats V1 mix by an average of 8%
results.quote: with our new mixture outperforming our old mixture by an average of 8%

results.claim: V2 mix gain shrinks with scale: 13% at 7B, 1% at 70B
results.quote: it only provides a 1% improvement at the 70B scale

results.claim: QLoRA lags full finetuning, mostly on AlpacaEval; gap shrinks with size
results.quote: (from 10% worse on average to 3% worse on average across

results.claim: CODE TÜLU 2 improves Codex-Eval by about 70% average over TÜLU 2 but drops AlpacaEval about 20%
results.setup: Code Llama vs LLaMA-2 on V2 mix
results.note: quote from the line-broken abstract bullet
text says 89.4 for GPT-3.5-turbo-0314, but Table 4 gives 83.6 for 0301

results.claim: TÜLU 2 70B is highest on average among open models in Table 1

limits: TruthfulQA omitted for DPO models because UltraFeedback uses TruthfulQA prompts (contamination).
Cannot rule out GPT models trained on benchmark data.
AlpacaEval and MT-Bench rely on a GPT-4 judge; GPT-4 version not pinned by AlpacaEval, authors fix GPT-4-0613.
No PPO or other RLHF comparison at scale; no data ablations of DPO; mechanisms not understood.
No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; QLoRA not tried at the DPO stage.
Training data mix lacks explicit multilingual data, which they suggest explains the TydiQA drop.
Code Llama-Instruct comparison confounded by its private training data.
Gains from the V2 mix cannot be attributed per dataset; no per-dataset ablation.

lineage.work: Zephyr: Direct distillation of LM alignment

lineage.note: result differs from Dettmers et al. on a wider task suite

lineage.work: A long way to go: length correlations in RLHF

figures.why: Shows the verbosity increase beside quality gains
